event.summary: Check removed xterm regressions against surviving terminal contracts
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: Removing the old renderer's query, selection and emoji tests may leave promised behavior without relevant checks while adopted old terminals still run. Details: assigned patches remove three direct-write Unicode tests and the DECRPM, DECRQSS and input-selection regressions. SPEC.md Terminal experience still permits adopted old terminals at this revision; SPEC_impl.md The grid client (1948 onward) distinguishes browser-side xterm parsing from supervisor-side interpretation for grid terminals. Existing grid test names and surviving Unicode replay cases suggest replacement coverage, but their assertions and query ownership still need inspection. Suggested bucket: other (test coverage only; no established product malfunction). Next checks: inspect surviving grid geometry/selection assertions and emulator query ownership, and determine whether legacy-only assertions retain an executable fixture. No execution or reproduction performed.

event.summary: Removed xterm assertions do not establish a terminal regression
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: The removed tests reduce coverage of the old terminal renderer while old terminals can still be adopted at this intermediate revision, but no source-supported product malfunction follows from the deletions. Details: all removed cases use OLD_TERMINAL_TAG and call xterm-specific parsing or selection APIs. The replacement grid does not parse program escape sequences: SPEC_impl.md, The grid client, 1950-1954 says the browser receives rows of styled runs and draws them; The supervisor's terminal emulator, 2842-2860 assigns interpretation and query answers to the supervisor. Existing e2e/grid-client/grid-terminal.spec.ts:199-243 verifies two-cell geometry and following-run placement; :245-371 verifies column ownership against font shaping; :1046-1079 uses real drags and separate typing/paste legs, asserts the selection premise, empty document selection, and sent key/paste messages. The surviving real-program Unicode tests, e2e/tests/terminal-unicode.spec.ts:109-140 and :151-192, verify narrow text presentation and replayed VS16/cursor alignment on grid terminals. No duplicate browser query responder exists in that replacement architecture. This is not a claim that legacy terminals retained runtime coverage: the commit explicitly removes their runnable fixture, and old terminals still supported here lose those checks until retired. Suggested bucket: other, test coverage only; no concrete user-impact route established. Could-be-highest: no; none of the removed assertions or inspected replacement contracts establishes security or loss-of-work harm. Confidence: confirmed source analysis of coverage and ownership; no runtime observation. proposed_drop: no actionable defect demonstrated by removing renderer-specific tests; source refutation is the split of query ownership and the surviving independent grid assertions above. possible_cover: none; coverage sources not searched. Lead settled by inspecting surviving assertions and the complete emulator/grid contract sections; no missing premise retained.

event.summary: Old-renderer regressions lose coverage before the supported renderer is retired
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513. TLDR: At this intermediate revision, existing sessions still use the old terminal renderer, but its query-reply, selection-dismissal and emoji regression checks are deleted. The later removal of the renderer ends the current need for those tests; it does not show the intermediate loss was harmless or that grid tests covered the old code. Details: SPEC.md:3016-3034 still promises that existing old terminals remain until the user moves them. The implementation still constructs xterm at crates/farhelm-ui/assets/terminal.js:3900, suppresses duplicate DECRQM replies at :4120-4128 and DECRQSS at :4144-4147, and clears both old-renderer/native selections through :4250-4295. These are precisely the safeguards exercised by the deleted terminal.spec.ts tests. The removed Unicode tests at parent revision e2e/tests/terminal-unicode.spec.ts:123-215 separately inspect wide/continuation cells, cursor-addressed redraws and the adjacent colored cell geometry in xterm's model/DOM. The same commit deletes e2e/suite-terminals.ts and removes the legacy test-run selection from playwright.config.ts; its deleted suite instructions explicitly said old terminals remain for sessions made by earlier versions and kept implementation-specific tests in their own run. Thus removal of the fixture and tests precedes removal of supported production paths. The independent grid geometry/selection tests at e2e/grid-client/grid-terminal.spec.ts:199-371 and :1046-1079, plus real-program grid Unicode replay at terminal-unicode.spec.ts:109-192, remain useful grid-specific observables; they neither call nor refute regressions in the retained xterm handlers. Cross-batch scope: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e later removes the old renderer/protocol branch, is an ancestor of pinned tip 00de0b6c9cf206f1a7c9c5ad1c76b5b10eaf85db, and its SPEC_impl.md:1842-1843 says every terminal mounts the grid. Pinned-tip source has no new Terminal, swallowDecrqm or registerDcsHandler in terminal.js and no vendor asset subtree; dismissSelectionSoon still appears as a generic attachment callback parameter, not the old implementation. Therefore this is a confirmed historical coverage gap, not a claim the pinned tip should restore xterm or has a current old-renderer bug. Suggested bucket: other, lost regression coverage in maintainer tooling; no new product malfunction or security/loss-of-work route established. Could-be-highest: no established route. Confidence: confirmed source/patch/contract analysis; no execution observation. proposed_drop: false. Preserve prior proposed drop verbatim in history: 'no actionable defect demonstrated by removing renderer-specific tests; source refutation is the split of query ownership and the surviving independent grid assertions above.' Synthesis rejects that rationale: absence of a new malfunction does not refute useful deleted regression tests, and grid ownership is not old-renderer coverage. Later complete retirement is a separate possible disposition reason for the parent, not an accepted drop; parent has accepted none. possible_cover: none; no queue or excluded-coverage search. No readily checkable premise remains open for this record.

event.summary: Mouse test claims to check SGR viewer restoration that the grid protocol does not carry
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: The mouse regression test now tells future maintainers it checks a reconnect failure that cannot occur in this architecture. It still usefully checks mouse input after reconnect, but does not test restoration of an SGR setting in the browser. Details: the newly rewritten rationale at e2e/tests/mouse-modes.spec.ts:390-395 says a bug dropping SGR encoding 'from what a reattached viewer is sent' would pass the earlier assertions and that the second reattach pins this branch. The wire contract has no such branch or field: crates/farhelm-proto/src/grid.rs:1098-1108 defines only off/click/drag/motion reporting modes, :1121-1148 defines the viewer's state, and :1632-1639 sends mouse coordinates/buttons without an encoding choice. The client explicitly documents that it cannot see the encoding at crates/farhelm-ui/assets/grid-terminal.js:1637-1648 and sends mouse messages based only on reporting mode. The supervisor input path uses its retained terminal modes (service/grid_stream.rs:1069-1077); grid_input.rs:737-745 selects SGR there. SPEC_impl.md, The grid client, assigns input encoding to that supervisor. Switching sessions at mouse-modes.spec.ts:397 does not restart that emulator or reconstruct its encoding state. The asserted counts at :399-405 therefore show that SGR reports still reach the program after a fresh browser attachment, not that SGR encoding was restored from viewer replay. Correct the rationale to describe that narrower contract; do not add an unnecessary encoding field or client encoder to satisfy it. The related old DECSET-replay wording at :357-358 is also stale, but the newly changed lines are the location for this finding. Suggested bucket: other, misleading test-coverage documentation without an established product failure. Could-be-highest: no security or loss-of-work route established. Confidence: confirmed by source and protocol analysis, no runtime observation. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; prohibited coverage sources were not searched. Original suspected consequence retained: false confidence in SGR restoration coverage; source checks settle that there is no viewer encoding state to restore, rather than demonstrating missing product functionality.

event.summary: Mouse test claims to check SGR viewer restoration that the grid protocol does not carry
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: The rewritten mouse-test rationale claims coverage of SGR encoding restored to a browser, although the browser never receives that encoding setting. The test remains useful for checking SGR mouse input after reattachment. Details: synthesis re-read the newly changed comment at e2e/tests/mouse-modes.spec.ts:390-395, the complete TerminalState definition at crates/farhelm-proto/src/grid.rs:1127-1153, and MouseMode at :1098-1108. Neither defines an SGR/default encoding field: state exposes off/click/drag/motion reporting and other display/focus/status fields. grid-terminal.js:1630-1648 produces coordinate/button messages based on reporting mode and explicitly says the client cannot see the encoding. service/grid_stream.rs:1064-1077 decodes the message, takes retained modes from its status receiver, and passes them to InputEncoder; grid_input.rs:737-745 selects SGR from modes.mouse_encoding. The changed comment specifically claims a regression 'dropped the SGR encoding ... from what a reattached viewer is sent' and that the second reconnect pins 'that branch'. No such viewer-encoding branch exists. The count assertion at mouse-modes.spec.ts:399-405 proves SGR reports reach the program following the new browser attachment. It can catch breakage of post-reattach mouse input; it does not establish browser SGR restoration, and does not restart the supervisor or rebuild its emulator from a checkpoint. Preserve the narrower original consequence: misleading coverage documentation can lead maintainers to believe the test exercises an SGR replay/restoration mechanism it does not exercise. Correct the rationale to its actual contract; no product field, client encoder, or new product functionality is missing on this evidence. Suggested bucket: other. Could-be-highest: no security or loss-of-work route established. Confidence: confirmed source/protocol/caller analysis, not runtime observation. proposed_drop: false; no lowering or drop made in synthesis. possible_cover: none, no queue search. Revision adds complete-state and direct-encoder rechecks without broadening the finding into a product defect.

event.summary: Mouse test claims to check SGR viewer restoration that the grid protocol does not carry
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: The rewritten mouse-test rationale claims coverage of SGR encoding restored to a browser, although the browser never receives that encoding setting. It still usefully checks SGR mouse input after reattachment. Details: the changed comment at e2e/tests/mouse-modes.spec.ts:390-395 claims to pin a branch that sends SGR encoding to a returning viewer. Complete TerminalState at crates/farhelm-proto/src/grid.rs:1127-1153 has no encoding field; MouseMode at :1098-1108 exposes only off/click/drag/motion. grid-terminal.js:1630-1648 builds coordinate/button messages and explicitly says the client cannot see encoding. service/grid_stream.rs:1064-1077 reads the retained terminal modes, and grid_input.rs:737-745 chooses SGR there. The test's :399-405 counts reports after switching session selection through reattachWithModes (:247-257), which closes/replaces only its browser socket. Additional synthesis caller/lifetime checks settle the remaining premise: service/handlers.rs:1898-1916 states the host runtime is already connected and creates HostAttach from terminal.clone(); grid_stream.rs:1022-1040 subscribes to that host's retained status and creates a fresh per-attachment InputEncoder. hosts/terminal.rs:1205-1227 establishes shared runtime ownership across cloned handles, backed by an Arc, separate from viewer attachment. Thus a new attachment/encoder is exercised, but no browser SGR field or emulator checkpoint restoration is exercised. Preserve original consequence: misleading coverage documentation can cause maintainers to believe this test exercises SGR viewer replay/restoration. Correct its rationale to post-reattach mouse delivery. Do not infer a missing product field, a need for a client encoder, or a product encoding defect. Related DECSET-replay wording at :357-358 is stale too, but the finding targets the newly changed rationale. Suggested bucket: other. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed protocol, implementation and caller/lifetime source analysis; no execution observation. proposed_drop: false; no lowering or accepted drop. possible_cover: none; no queue/excluded metadata search. This revision records the actual runtime/attachment boundary and preserves the narrower coverage-documentation consequence; no premise remains open.

event.summary: Grid fit formula and retained assertions agree after component removal
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: Considered whether simplifying the two-renderer fit test introduced incorrect pixel-ratio rounding or carried a prior fitted answer into later sizes. Source checks refute that concern. Details: the changed documentation specifies a fixed 80x24 reference. fittedSizes at :238 keeps that reference const, :245-246 rounds after dividing the full reference canvas by dpr, and :248-249 applies padding/scrollbar and dimension bounds. Production grid-terminal.js:222-227 computes deviceWidth=charWidth*dpr and returns Math.round(deviceWidth*cols/dpr)/cols, with height likewise rounding the reference canvas; this matches the test's parenthesization, rather than rounding individual device cells and dividing afterward. Production :242-245 applies the same independently stated bounds and scrollbar reserve. Test :265 checks actual pixel ratio; :272-276 checks font metric availability, padding, positive width and fitted rows/columns. No new formula mismatch or feedback of prior answers was established. Suggested bucket: other if such a test defect existed; candidate only. Could-be-highest: no established security/loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed source refutation, no execution observation. proposed_drop: the candidate rounding/reference concern is refuted by the exact implementation and assertion references above; pending parent disposition, no accepted drop implied. possible_cover: none; neighbour records were read only for novelty, no prohibited coverage search. This is a considered-and-refuted discovery check, not a new finding or an assertion that matching production alone proves every sizing behavior.
